title: I2 (anonymous-only fallback): bounded joint-motion residual on the incumbent, searched then qualified on fresh pairs
hypothesis: Bounded reinforcement of filtered joint motion sustains effective movement through slow-spin tails without increasing drops. (The original contact-residual prediction is UNTESTED: R-097 / D-069 failed the rolling decoder gate, so the contact arm is not run.)

prediction.against: the unchanged D-058 fixed-stroke incumbent on the same 90 fresh paired cases (seed 4744)
prediction.rationale: The frozen winner of a 24-draw random search of a four-parameter anonymous joint-motion residual should lift fresh paired sustained success by at least +0.10 over the incumbent; S1 of R-097 showed the incumbent's failures are steady low-rate rolling (42 of 52), which stronger joint motion could plausibly raise.

code_changes: Module lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/incumbent_residual.py, config block incumbent_residual (incumbent_residual_fresh merged from it), two registry names in scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py, mocked unittest tests/test_incumbent_residual.py. Stage 3, the unchanged config/pen_spin/d058_fixed_stroke_incumbent, one whole manifest per fresh Isaac process, serial, no LLM, no retries, no extra draws. The contact arm is not run or tuned.

Residual (JointMotionResidual), reading the 20 actuated joints' observed velocities and anonymous indices only (no fingertip geometry, no pen frame, no roll sign): v_f <- v_f + alpha (v - v_f) with alpha = dt / (tau + dt); delta = clip(g * sign(v_f) * max(|v_f| - v0, 0), -b, b) in rad; action = clamp(incumbent + 2 delta / (hi - lo), -1, 1). With g = 0 the action equals the incumbent's exactly (unit-tested). Four free scalars: g in [0, 0.10] s, v0 in [0, 0.50] rad/s, tau in [0.05, 0.25] s, b in [0.25 B, B].

Cap: B = 0.15 rad, so b in [0.0375, 0.15] rad. This replaces the fallback's earlier B = 0.02 rad, for reasons stated before any episode: 0.02 rad is about 6% of the incumbent's stroke (0.28 x 1.408 = 0.39 normalised, about 0.3 rad), while the only change that ever qualified on this incumbent (D-058) scaled the stroke by 41%, so a null at 0.02 rad would be uninformative; B = 0.15 rad is R-097's frozen per-joint increment cap, under which pulses changed no episode length and added no drop. D-069 also measured the incumbent's action saturated on MFJ2 (79%) and LFJ1 (64%), where an additive residual is clipped; the fraction of residual values clipped by the action clamp is reported per cell.

S3 (`--study incumbent_residual`, 80 + 24 x 80 = 2,000 episodes, a stop point): the incumbent once and 24 draws on the frozen 80-case probe manifest (seed 4742). Draws are numpy.random.default_rng(4743) uniform in the declared ranges, written to draws.json before the first cell. Ranking: mean final-window hit fraction, then sustained successes, then the lower draw index. The report gives, for the incumbent and every draw: successes, tail-hit fraction, timeout rate, drops, slow-spin and off-centre counts, mean unsigned roll integral (rad), residual activity (mean |delta|, fraction at the cap, fraction clipped by the action clamp). The winner's parameters and their sha256 are written to selected.json and then into the config (selected / selected_sha256). S3 then STOPS: the report is returned to the advisor for agreement, and no fresh case runs before that.

S4 (`--study incumbent_residual_fresh`, 2 x 90 = 180 episodes): refuses to run unless the config's selected block matches selected_sha256 and S3's recorded winner. The incumbent and the frozen winner on the 90-case fresh manifest (seed 4744), paired by case. Primary: paired sustained-success difference with its 95% t interval; adoption needs mean > 0 and lower bound > 0 (a tie never promotes) AND the one-sided 95% upper bound of the paired drop-rate difference <= +0.05 (one comparison, so no multiplicity correction). Also reported: win/loss/tie, paired final-window hit-fraction difference, drops, slow-spin and off-centre counts, unsigned roll, residual activity.

Scope of any conclusion: this one residual family, this incumbent, one 24-draw random search. A null shelves this joint-motion-reinforcement family only. No BC, RL, curriculum, gradient fitting, automatic new draws or controller revisions after outcomes.

falsified_by: A fresh paired sustained-success interval whose upper bound is below +0.10 refutes the predicted magnitude; an interval including zero establishes no improvement. Adoption additionally requires the strict paired rule (mean > 0 and 95% lower bound > 0) and a one-sided 95% upper bound of the paired drop-rate difference <= +0.05.

selected.rule: mean final-window hit fraction, then sustained successes, then the lower index

controls.contact_arm: not run: R-097 (D-069) failed the rolling decoder gate; the original contact prediction is untested

result.notes: Episodes: S3 2,000 (incumbent 80 + 24 x 80) on probe seed 4742, S4 180 (2 x 90) on fresh seed 4744; 0 LLM generation calls; about 20 minutes on the box. Probe-to-fresh shrinkage as expected for the best of 24: +0.100 on the probe cases (39 vs 31 of 80), +0.056 on fresh (41 vs 36 of 90). Deviation: the first S4 invocation crashed after the incumbent's cell and before the residual's cell ran, because the driver wrote its frozen-winner record to selected.json, the filename of the `selected` controller's cell, so that cell was skipped as existing; the record was renamed frozen_selected.json, the driver fixed, and S4 resumed (the incumbent's cell was reused, not rerun). No fresh result for the residual existed before the fix, and nothing was retuned. Secondary, not the registered metric: on fresh the residual raises mean unsigned roll from 22.0 to 28.0 rad and mean |axial rate| from 3.89 to 4.90 rad/s, with slow-spin failures 44 vs 48, with a mean |delta| of 0.0066 rad (clipped by the action clamp on 0.3% of values). In S3 22 of 24 draws raised unsigned roll and 13 had zero drops against the incumbent's 3; the low-gain draws led and the largest-gain draws were worst. No interval was computed for the roll difference. Power: the paired SE is 0.048, so this 90-pair instrument resolves about +/-0.10; a true effect near +0.05 cannot be established or excluded by it.

verdicts.reasoning: By the registered rule the prediction (+0.10 paired sustained success over the incumbent on 90 fresh pairs) is neither supported nor refuted: +0.056, 95% interval [-0.041, +0.152], which contains both zero and +0.10 (41 vs 36 of 90; 12 wins, 7 losses, 71 ties). The residual does not promote (lower bound below zero) and is not adopted; the drop bound holds (1 vs 1, upper bound 0.0 <= 0.05). No improvement is established. It is not a refutation either: the upper bound is above the threshold, and the secondaries point the same way as the point estimate (unsigned roll 28.0 vs 22.0 rad, tail-hit +0.048 [-0.046, +0.142], 22 of 24 probe draws raising roll), but those are not the registered metric and the roll difference has no interval. The instrument resolves about +/-0.10, so an effect near +0.05 is below what it can decide. Scope: this joint-motion-reinforcement family, this incumbent, one 24-draw search; the contact arm was not run.
verdicts.next_experiment: Do not adopt. The cheapest decisive step is a prospective replication of the SAME frozen residual (hash 2a509ef5...) on a larger fresh paired instrument sized for +0.05 (about 360 pairs for SE 0.024), with no retuning, as D-057 did for the curl clamp; otherwise shelve this family. R-098 stays deferred (its precondition, a passing decoder gate, did not occur).

verdicts.reasoning: Against the unchanged incumbent, fresh paired_success_difference was +0.0556 with a 95% interval of [-0.0405, +0.1516], from 41 versus 36 successes across 90 pairs [logs/pen_spin/r099_incumbent_residual/fresh_summary.json]. The interval includes both zero and the predicted +0.10, so no improvement is established and the predicted magnitude is neither supported nor refuted [logs/pen_spin/r099_incumbent_residual/fresh_summary.json]. The recorded drop-rate upper bound was 0.000, satisfying the +0.05 safety bound, but the success interval fails the strict promotion rule; the incumbent remains unchanged [logs/pen_spin/r099_incumbent_residual/fresh_summary.json].

direction: No LLM calls in any protocol. Test bounded residual repairs of the working fixed-stroke incumbent (config/pen_spin/d058_fixed_stroke_incumbent) on Stage 3, in four separately gated steps: (S1) reproduce the incumbent on fixed cases and quantify its slow-spin failures, with angular progress measured along each case's own roll direction; (S2) qualify the contact-frame decoder DURING ROLLING on top of the incumbent stroke, reporting requested, feasible (after bounds and least squares) and achieved motion separately, with tracking error, directional agreement and bound activity as pass/fail criteria (controllability gate); (S3) only if S2 passes, compare incumbent alone, a hand-authored contact-frame residual and a hand-authored anonymous-coordinate joint residual, with matched tuning budgets (same parameter count, same number of probe evaluations, same tuning method, tuned on probe cases and frozen before any fresh case), candidates ranked by tail-hit fraction with sustained unsigned angular progress and retention inspected; (S4) evaluate the selected controllers on fresh paired cases, 90 pairs per comparison, Holm correction over the two comparisons, promotion requires the strict paired sustained-success rule AND a pre-declared numeric non-inferiority bound on drops (usefulness gate). Residuals must not assume a roll sign. If S2 fails, the anonymous residual may still be compared against the incumbent alone. A failed hand-authored controller shelves that decoder/controller family only. No BC, RL, curriculum or gradient fitting. One protocol at a time on the box.

advisor.reasoning: The matched four-parameter, 24-draw search and fresh paired usefulness gate fit S3/S4, but spending 4,190 episodes and zero LLM calls must wait for R-097; decoder failure with intact reproduction permits only the declared 2,180-episode anonymous fallback. Its weakest point is that the primary endpoint tests contact versus incumbent, not superiority over the anonymous controller, which requires the secondary paired comparison to exclude zero. Retain the paired_success_difference prediction of an increase of at least 0.10 against the unchanged incumbent on 90 fresh paired cases; falsified_by is an interval upper bound below +0.10, and neither an interval including zero nor failure of the corrected promotion or drop bound permits adoption.

implementer.reasoning: Defer until R-097 is decided; the contact arm's cap B and pulse amplitude come from R-097's frozen block, and a decoder failure switches it to the anonymous-only fallback. The secondary contact-minus-anonymous comparison must exclude zero before any claim about contact coordinates.

advisor.reasoning: I accept the implementer's conditional argument: D-069 reproduces the incumbent but fails rolling-decoder qualification, activating only the declared anonymous-only fallback. Reinforcing observed joint motion could repair low-rate tails without assuming a roll sign, but it might instead amplify ineffective motion. The remaining defects are that the hypothesis and prediction concern the now-ineligible contact arm, and the combined invocation does not explicitly preserve the user's separate S3 and S4 gates.

State falsified_by: a paired interval upper bound below +0.10 refutes the predicted magnitude; an interval including zero establishes no improvement. Mark the original contact prediction untested.

Separate execution gates: S3 costs 2,000 episodes (80 incumbent plus 24 x 80 anonymous probes), then stop and record the selected controller's hash, tail-hit ranking, sustained unsigned progress, retention, saturation and drops for S4 review. Do not execute any fresh cases before that gate.

Declare S4 separately at 180 episodes, retaining the fallback's strict positive paired sustained-success interval and one-sided 95% paired drop-rate upper bound <= +0.05. Total maximum remains 2,180 episodes and zero LLM calls, with no additional draws or retuning.

implementer.reasoning: Agree to revise, and agree with the advisor's four changes (anonymous-only executable protocol on seeds 4742/4743/4744, hypothesis and prediction restated as anonymous residual minus the unchanged incumbent with the contact prediction marked untested, S3 as a 2,000-episode stop point reporting the selected hash and its ranking/progress/retention/saturation/drops, S4 declared separately at 180 episodes with the strict paired rule and a one-sided 95% drop bound <= +0.05). One further change, with new evidence from D-069: the fallback cap B = 0.02 rad was written before S2 and makes a null uninformative. The incumbent's stroke is 0.28 x 1.408 = 0.39 in normalised action, about 0.3 rad on a 1.57 rad joint range, so a 0.02 rad residual is about 6% of the stroke, while the one change that ever qualified on this incumbent (D-058) scaled the stroke by 41%; and D-069 measured that the incumbent's action is already saturated on MFJ2 (79%) and LFJ1 (64%), where any additive residual is clipped anyway. I propose B = 0.15 rad, which is not a new tuned number: it is the per-joint increment cap R-097 froze from its calibration (cal2) and under which pulses changed no episode length and caused no extra drop. The cap range stays [0.25 B, B] = [0.0375, 0.15] rad; everything else in the fallback is unchanged. The S3 report will include the fraction of steps on which the residual was clipped by the action clamp.

advisor.reasoning: I accept the implementer's argument for predeclaring B = 0.15 rad rather than 0.02 rad: it permits a meaningful intervention relative to the incumbent stroke, although brief pulse retention does not establish safety for sustained motion reinforcement. The revised anonymous-only fallback tests whether reinforcing filtered joint motion repairs slow-spin tails without assuming roll direction, reusing scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml for 2,000 S3 episodes and zero LLM calls. Retain the prediction paired_success_difference, direction increase, threshold 0.10, against the unchanged D-058 incumbent on the same 90 fresh paired cases; it is falsified by an interval upper bound below +0.10, and an interval including zero establishes no improvement. Approve S3 now with its mandatory stop and frozen winner hash; the additional 180-episode, zero-LLM S4 remains gated on review of tail-hit ranking, sustained progress, retention and residual activity, with adoption requiring the strict positive paired interval and paired drop-rate upper bound <= +0.05.

implementer.reasoning: Approve as revised: anonymous-only, four parameters, 24 seeded draws, cap range [0.0375, 0.15] rad, S3 a 2,000-episode stop point with the winner hashed, S4 gated on the advisor's review of the S3 report, strict paired rule plus the drop bound. A pass on short pulses does not establish that sustained reinforcement is safe, which is exactly what S3's drop counts will show.
